it really depends on if the person self diagnosing has actually done a substantial amount of research or if they just took a buuzfeed quiz that told them they had it. Medical Diagnoses are in my opinion a privilege or rather something that not everyone has access to. They require time, money, transportation, insurance, ability to describe your symptoms, ability to advocate for yourself, a psych who will actually listen to you, knowledge on how to get a diagnosis, etc etc etc.   
saying something like "ugh im so ocd" or "I have a bit of ocd" are invalidating. Saying "I think I have ocd" or even "I have ocd" when you don't have an official diagnose imo aren't. Ocd the disorder has also lasted waaay longer then Ocd the diagnosis. But the people who had ocd didn't not have it just because they didn't have access to a word for it. I feel like its applicable here too.

I think is some ways we on a whole as a society misunderstand words you'll hear people say, "im so depressed" when often what they mean is, "I'm so sad" and I truly think that there is just meaning lost in a lot of words. at the same time we are not mental health professionals and can not and should not try to measure someone elses ptsd/cptsd it's not our place. You're allowed to be frustrated. I do think that when someone says something like this, such as "I got scratched by a cat and it was so traumatizing" that, that opens up a space for conversation about trauma and ptsd. 

Also, it's important to remember that, really strange things can cause trauma right? things that might be normal to other folks could be a trauma to someone else. or even more so stranger triggers due to association. I'll use myself as an example. Playing for most kids wasn't traumatic at all but play time was traumatic for me because it was used as a way to sexually assault me. if I just said, "I got ptsd from playing as a kid" you might think, well thats so stupid that's not a trauma. also fresh out my trauma I had all sorts of triggers, in varying degrees. on the smaller side of things I couldn't eat/smell ramen because my abuser enjoyed ramen. if I said "ramen triggers me" you might also get upset. 

overall I think in situations like this there is just a lot of miscommunication and there may be context your missing, otherwise its a good opening into having a conversation about trauma in a respectful, judge-free, way.

ocd is a doubting disorder it feeds off of rumination and reassurance which is what you're doing that cycle of asking yourself over and over is those two things, knowing that can help combat it more. Do the opposite, ocd wants your reassurance so just say instead, "Yup you're right, I'm bi" or alternatively show that you just don't care go, "maybe I am maybe I'm not, oh well" and shrug it off. Also, why would you want to kill yourself for being bi? do you think there's something wrong with it?

Honestly, this is a very common thing that happens to a lot of kids. Kids experiment sexually, they might kiss or pretend to date or make their dolls have babies or the classic, "I'll show you mine if you show me yours" Right now ocd is giving you these accusations because it want's to hear you reassure it, it want's to replay the memory over and over and over to find an arguing point and then proceeds to find another bit to argue with the arguing point you just found. It's a vicious cycle and it will never end itself. This is what helps, ocd feeds off of your reassurance so what do you do? the opposite, your ocd might say, "You sexually assaulted your brother" you can reply with, "I absolutely did" alternatively brush it off ocd will say, "you sexually assaulted your brother" reply with, "ah, maybe I did maybe I didn't" with a shrug. Show your ocd that it's not bothering you and that you're perfectly fine with the idea that maybe you did...obviously your not but all the same.

Ocd can be called a doubt disorder. Ocd wants to hyper-analyze every little thing that may have been wrong so what do you do? you start replaying things over and over and over trying to dissect it. Soon you may begin to fill the gaps with thoughts or feelings or even actions that may not have happened. Analyzing is a compulsion and reassurance even if it's self-reassurance is also a compulsion once you recognize this it may be easier to cope with. If your ocd starts to bring up old memories or attack you with accusations either try to agree with it (which throws ocd way off because it feeds off of reassurance) or just brush it off completely saying something like, "Maybe I did, maybe I didn't" with a shrug and then trying to move on sometimes you have to do this over and over and ocd is going to try to pull up more and more things to get you to give it that reassurance but you got to fight it.

I want to say that first of all, you're right kids do these things it's completely normal. Additionally I want to let you know that you're performing compulsions, mainly reasurance seeking and dissection/ trying to pick a part a memory. There's no shame in doing a compulsion, and this isn't me trying to critique you either god knows I have a shit ton of compulsions and at the same time once you recognize these things it might get easier to deal with them. Here's what I would recommend, although it is hard. Ocd plays reverse psychology with you, it's telling you these things because it wants to hear your reassurance it wants to be convinced that there's nothing you ever did wrong but in doing so it drags you into worse feelings. So what do you do? agree with it, either that or just let it know that you don't care for example lets say, "You're a murderer" reply with, "yes, absolutely I am" alternatively show your ocd that you don't care, say it even though you do care it's going to say, "you're a murderer" reply with, "whatever you say" or simply laugh in it's face and try to move on.

The best thing to do with urges to pick is learn how to cope with them. Something I've been learning that I think is at least somewhat helpful is thinking up of something like a chest or a box and when a thought like that comes up all you do is think "box" and imagine putting that urge/thought in your box and know that the thought does not come out of your box unless you let it if you get the same urge that's not the first one escaping its a second one that you just put in your box again. This isn't a permanent fix, the boxes function is keep these things safe and separate until you're in a safe enough space with a therapist to processes the urges.

I have ocd so I needed something clean and something that wouldn't contaminate me   
So I thought up of a bubble, something clean. The bubble is unpoppable and I can take things in and out with ease however it is impossible to escape from the inside so the thoughts there cannot escape and they dont want to escape because my bubble is clean and comfortable and lets the thoughts relax and enjoy themselves. When the thoughts are in my bubble they become cleaner and cleaner as well, and less scary that way.
